subject: Post-demo: Forensics evidence delivery format, residency and retention
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Forensics evidence delivery format, residency and retention

Hi Sanjay / Emily —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of the evidence items you asked Redwood to provide so your security & legal teams can validate our "who/what/when" access evidence for the pilot: 

- Primary ask: export of access events covering the pilot timeframe (90 days) that show who accessed protected content and when (user id, role, action, resource id, request_id, timestamp, source IP, region).
- Desired formats: CSV or JSONL; parquet is acceptable for large exports but they prefer CSV for quick review.
- Retention & residency: confirmation of default retention policy (180 days) and whether historical exports can be scoped to only US regions (we can filter by region tag).
- Transfer method: secure transfer (pre-signed S3 link OR SFTP) and an MD5/SHA256 checksum for each file.
- Pseudonymization: Emily asked whether user identifiers can be pseudonymized for sensitive datasets; we'll note options (hashed user_id, provide mapping under NDA).

I've attached a short sample CSV (access_log_sample.csv) with anonymized/example rows and a 1-page SOC2 summary for context.

Next steps we propose: 
1) Marcus to confirm the export schema and column naming that we'll produce (CSV/JSONL exact header names).
2) Marcus to confirm transfer options and earliest ETA for a 7-day sample export.
3) Legal (Emily) to confirm if they need an additional DPA amendment or evidence acceptance form signed.

Can you confirm the time range you want in the 7-day sample (most security teams ask for the most recent 7 days)? Also, confirm whether you want IPs redacted.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: access_log_sample.csv (stub, 320 KB, anonymized), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (stub, 180 KB)

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finsecure.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.legal@finsecure.com>, FinSecure Security Ops <secops@finsecure.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Forensics evidence delivery format, residency and retention

Neha —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before Marcus prepares the sample export: 

- Time range: yes, please send the most recent rolling 7 days for the sample. If possible include a separate sample covering a single anomalous session (we can indicate the request_id after we get the first sample).
- Pseudonymization: Legal would prefer hashed user_id in the sample, but they will want the mapping under NDA only if we proceed to a full export. For the sample, please hash the user_id and keep original role values (admin/dev/user).
- IPs: include them; our team will handle IP-level review internally. If export can include geolocation (region tag) that helps scope residency.
- Column headers: can you confirm exact names? We prefer snake_case.
- Transfer: pre-signed S3 is fine. Include SHA256 checksums.

Emily — looping you in for the DPA question — do we need an amendment for this limited evidence exchange or will the existing DPA cover it?

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Security | FinSecure, Inc.
---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finsecure.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Forensics evidence delivery format, residency and retention

Sanjay / Neha —

Thanks — below are the concrete export details we can produce out-of-the-box and what will require configuration: 

1) Export formats supported (out-of-the-box): CSV (comma-delimited, UTF-8, LF), JSONL (newline-delimited JSON). Parquet export available for large archives but we'll stick to CSV for the sample.

2) CSV schema (snake_case header names):
   - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
   - request_id (uuid)
   - user_id_hash (sha256 hex)
   - role (admin|dev|user|service_account)
   - action (read|write|delete|list|cache_read|cache_write)
   - resource_id (string)
   - resource_type (model|embedding|file)
   - ip_address (v4/v6)
   - region (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1)
   - kv_cache_key (nullable)
   - response_code (http-like numeric)

   Example row (anonymized):
   2027-05-01T22:14:03Z, 9f1c2e4a-..., 4c2f9d..., admin, read, model:llama-13b, model, 54.187.22.11, us-east-1, , 200

3) Pseudonymization: we will produce user_id_hash (sha256 from user_id). If FinSecure needs the mapping, that is available under NDA and a controlled request.

4) Retention & residency: Redwood default retention for access events is 180 days in hosted mode. We can scope exports by region tag; however, note that some multi-region fallbacks may have cross-region metadata. For the sample we will filter to us-east-1 only.

5) Transfer: we can provide a pre-signed S3 PUT/GET link with a 7-day expiry. Files will be accompanied by a sidecar file checksums.sha256. For very sensitive transfers we can do SFTP into a customer-managed endpoint (requires network allowance).

ETA: We can produce the 7-day CSV sample (hashed user_id) within 48 hours if you confirm the exact 7-day window.

Attachments: I'm attaching the anonymized access_log_sample.csv (same as Neha attached) and a short forensics checklist (forensics-pack-checklist.md) describing packaging and manifest format.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: access_log_sample.csv (stub, 320 KB), forensics-pack-checklist.md (stub, 6 KB)

From: Emily Chen <emily.legal@finsecure.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finsecure.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Forensics evidence delivery format, residency and retention

Neha / Marcus —

Thanks for the schema and clear options. A couple legal points: 

- For the sample: hashed user_id is fine. We do not need mapping for the sample.
- For a full export (if the pilot proceeds), we will need a short DPA amendment to reflect the export mechanics and retention expectations. I can draft a one-paragraph amendment and share a DocuSign link — please let me know if Redwood has a standard export addendum.
- Please do not include any raw PII fields in the sample. If you believe a field could contain PII (e.g., resource name referencing a user email), remove or hash it.

If Redwood can deliver the sample by end-of-day Wednesday (2027-05-04) that would be ideal for our review.

Best,
Emily Chen
Senior Counsel | FinSecure, Inc.
---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

All —

Confirmed: Marcus will run the export scoped to us-east-1, most recent 2027-04-27 to 2027-05-03 (7 days) and produce CSV with the schema he listed, user_id hashed (sha256), IPs included, any resource fields that look like emails will be hashed/removed per Emily's guidance.

ETA: sample CSV + checksums + manifest (manifest.jsonl) will be uploaded to a pre-signed S3 link by 2027-05-04 EOD PST. I will share the link once available and add a short readme describing the manifest and checksum file.

Action items: 
- Marcus: produce and upload sample by EOD 5/4.
- Emily: if you need an amendment, please share the draft; we can route to Legal (Lauren) and get back quickly.
- Sanjay: once you validate the sample we can scope the full 180-day export and agree transfer cadence.

Thanks — will follow up with the S3 link shortly.

Neha
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
